newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Suspension helps Shenzhen shares up amid crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Suspension helps Shenzhen shares up amid crackdown.

text.p: Shenzhen's indices ended Friday morning higher despite a government securities crackdown, saved by the suspension of heavily index-weighted Shenzhen Development Bank, traders said.
The domestic currency A share index gained 5.31 points or 1.29 percent to 418.22 after opening down 5.67 percent. Turnover was 3.1 billion yuan.
The foreign currency B share index was almost unchanged at 143.36 points, up 0.03 or 0.02 percent on thin turnover of HK$17.5 million.
"The A share market was spared a dive thanks to the Shenzhen bank's suspension," a trader at China Guotai Securities said.

The Shenzhen Stock Exchange suspended trading in the shares of the country's only domestically listed bank after Beijing announced it was being punished for illegally trading in its own shares, violating securities rules.
Bank Chairman He Yun has been sacked and all bank earnings from trading in its own shares has been confiscated, the official media said. Bank officials declined to comment.
Brokers also said shares gained because investors had largely digested the news already.

It was one of a series of announcements made after the markets closed on Thursday, including an order to remove heads of three top brokerages and ban the brokerages from trading on their own accounts for one year.
Beijing last week ordered all state banks to unwind their stock market positions within 10 sessions to reduce the inflow of speculative funds to China's over-heated stock markets.
The ban follows recent moves to ban state and listed firms from speculative stock trading.
Analysts said this may not be the end of the government's efforts to still stock speculation.
"Any strong rebound may trigger new crackdown measures," an analyst at China Securities Co said.
"Beijing has a bunch of crackdown measures at hand, it is just a matter of when it decides to pepper them into the markets," she said.
On the B share market, the biggest gainer was Jiangling Motors Corp which rose HK$0.20 or 5.56 percent to HK$3.80.
The best A share performer was Xinjiang Hong Yuan Trust, which added 1.06 yuan or 8.56 percent to 13.45 yuan.
